accepted: Theorem 1: complete N=2 interval classification for nondegenerate positive intervals whose closure contains 1, including finite and infinite endpoints, threshold uniqueness, equality and attainment qualifications
Imported example lambda=(3,3), mu=(4,1): sharp B=1+sqrt(2) threshold for [1,B]^2

Theorem 2: exact endpoint-quotient criterion for the single N=3 pair lambda=(5,1,1), mu=(4,3,0), all nonempty positive intervals, sharp cubic rho, exact certificate, endpoint and equality classification
Common rectangle shifts to positive ordinary partitions and the corresponding strict exponent tuples
Proposition 3: general N log-ratio lower bound and sufficient strict one-sided radii under the stated degree sign and denominator-degree conditions
Proposition 4: equal-degree covariance-difference sufficient and obstructing local sign test, plus exact covariance moments for the specified N=3 pair

reason: The original bounded-interval Schur-ratio task asks for a classification for arbitrary partition pairs and dimensions. The PR proves a complete N=2 classification only for intervals whose closure contains1, one exact N=3 pair with a sharp cubic endpoint quotient, and general sufficient one-sided/covariance local tests. It does not classify arbitrary N>=3 pairs, arbitrary intervals even inN2, general sharp radii or the zero-covariance case. Its explicit Bernstein certificate proves the special pair rather than a general vertex-minimum reduction. Prior orthant majorization uses unbounded scaling, which does not provide the missing finite-box converse. No full original-target claim is inferred.
